name: veridian-cockpit
description: The Veridian Cockpit - the VS Code client for Veridian. Run a sandbox validation, read the verdict, open the evidence it was reached from, and show the twin: every run on disk joined into one row by subject. Veridian builds twelve reproducible sandbox worlds - some real, some a substitute for one - records which limits each world can actually enforce, and decides whether the software works; a world that cannot justify a verdict is reported INCONCLUSIVE rather than passed. The same engine is behind the veridian CLI, a CI job and a Model Context Protocol surface, so this is one client of it rather than the only way in. The coding agent stays external and never decides whether it succeeded.

commands.title: Veridian: Resolve the definition and show the transcript
Veridian: Measure M1..M5 over the runs on disk
Veridian: Show the twin - every run, joined by subject
Veridian: Open the last failure report

veridian.cli.description: Path to the Veridian CLI entry point. Empty means: resolve it from the workspace (node_modules/.bin, then cli/veridian.ts), then `npx --no-install veridian`.

veridian.goal.description: Goal document the commands run against, relative to the workspace folder or absolute. Empty means: the active file if it is a goal, then goal.yaml in the workspace folder.

veridian.stateDir.description: Where run bundles are written, relative to the workspace folder. The same default the CLI uses.

veridian.browser.description: Passed to the CLI as --browser. `none` makes every browser observation INCONCLUSIVE, which is the loop refusing to judge, not a failure.

scripts.gate: npm run typecheck && npm test && npm run build && npm run smoke:out
